attacks.claim: `--version vX.Y.Z` lets any user install any older release that still carries a valid signature, including versions with known security defects such as the v2.6.2 credential-logging bug the plan cites. The plan has no minimum-version floor, no warning, and no revocation list for vulnerable releases, so signature validity alone does not mean the installed version is safe.
attacks.evidence: Command: kvx self-update [--check] [--version vX.Y.Z]; "the archive is rejected unless the signature verifies"; ABSENT: any downgrade protection, advisory check, or known-bad version list for --version and --rollback
